stem: An average-risk client asks whether performing a formal breast self-exam every month can replace recommended screening mammography. Which response is most accurate according to current American Cancer Society guidance?

options.A: Yes. Regular breast self-exam is an equivalent substitute for screening mammography in average-risk adults.
options.B: No. Routine breast self-exam is not recommended as a breast-cancer screening method for average-risk women; the client should follow recommended mammography screening and report new breast changes promptly.
options.C: Yes. Clinical breast examination and breast self-examination are both required in addition to every screening mammogram for average-risk women.
options.D: No breast awareness is useful between mammograms, so new lumps or other changes can wait until the next scheduled screening.

rationale: The American Cancer Society states that research has not shown a clear benefit from regular breast self-exams or clinical breast exams as routine screening in average-risk women and does not recommend them as part of the routine screening schedule. ACS does advise women to be familiar with how their breasts normally look and feel and to report changes promptly. Mammography remains the recommended screening modality; self-exam does not replace it.
educational_objective: Distinguish breast awareness from formal breast self-examination and explain that self-exam does not replace recommended mammography screening in average-risk women.
source_document_title: American Cancer Society Recommendations for the Early Detection of Breast Cancer
source_version_date: Current ACS breast cancer screening guideline page; accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: Section 'Clinical breast exam (CBE) and breast self-exam (BSE)': no clear benefit of regular CBE/BSE; not recommended as routine screening for average-risk women; women should be familiar with normal breast appearance/feel and report changes promptly
source_claim_supported: ACS does not recommend routine breast self-exam or clinical breast exam as routine breast-cancer screening for average-risk women, while encouraging familiarity with normal breast appearance/feel and prompt reporting of changes; mammography is the recommended screening modality.

correction_summary: Corrected the original implication that formal breast self-exam is a recommended complement to clinical breast exam and mammography. Current ACS guidance does not recommend routine BSE or CBE for average-risk women. The revised item distinguishes breast awareness/reporting changes from formal self-examination and preserves mammography as the screening modality.
